label: Gmail
what: How many important messages are unread, and the newest few senders and subjects.

credentials.label: Google client id
credentials.help: From a Google Cloud OAuth client of type Desktop app.

credentials.label: Google client secret
credentials.looks: A short string that usually starts with GOCSPX-

reads: Unread important mail from the last 7 days, not Promotions or Social.
For each message only the sender, the subject and the date.
not_reads: Anything you have already read, and your sent mail.
steps: Open the Google Cloud console and create a project, or pick one you already have.
Turn on the Gmail API for that project.
Set up the OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform in newer consoles). Choose External for a personal Gmail account and add your own address as a test user.
Create credentials of type OAuth client ID. Choose the application type Desktop app.
Publish the app: on the consent screen set the publishing status to In production. While it stays in Testing, Google expires the sign-in token after 7 days and Gmail stops until you sign in again.

Google may show an unverified-app warning for your own account. That is expected for a personal app: choose Advanced, then continue. Do this publish step before you sign in, because a token made in Testing keeps the 7-day limit.
Copy the client id and the client secret into the two fields here and save each one.
Press Save on the second value. Quarterdeck then opens the Google sign-in for you: pick your account and approve read-only access. For a second account use Add another account and do the same.
The sign-in token is kept beside the credentials file, readable by you only. If no tab opens, press Continue with Google on the card.
Switch Gmail on. If it later says the token expired or was revoked, press Sign in with Google again.
revoke: In your Google Account, open Security, then Third-party access, pick the app and remove access. Then remove both fields here and delete ~/.config/quarterdeck/google-gmail-token.json.
tested: Parsing tested against sample data only; not tested against the real service.
